title: Uniqueness of the stationary uniform distribution
statement: Let $G$ be a finite nonempty $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$. Suppose $G$ is connected and nonbipartite. For a rational-valued function $p$ on the vertices whose values sum to $1$, call $p$ stationary if one step of the walk preserves it: for every vertex $v$, $\sum_u p(u)P(u,v)=p(v)$, where $P(u,v)$ is the probability that a uniformly chosen indexed neighbor of $u$ is $v$. Then $p$ is stationary if and only if $p(v)=1/|V(G)|$ for every vertex $v$.
